correctness.rationale: The Crofton motion-invariant line measure of lines hitting a convex polygon is its perimeter; a segment has hit measure twice its length. For adjacent sides AB and BC, their union of hit-line sets equals the hit-line set of triangle ABC almost everywhere; inclusion-exclusion gives joint measure |AB|+|BC|-|AC|. Thus normalized side lengths a_i=m_i/2 and two-step chords b_i=a_i+a_{i+1}-q_i, whose cosine law uniquely fixes all interior angles. Positive turns summing to 2pi plus vector closure with lengths a_i give a strictly convex closed polygon and are necessary/sufficient. Compact strict angle/side lower bounds imply inverse local Lipschitzness; equilateral lengths make m_i=2/n. Independently computed random convex polygon side incidence by angular quadrature; maximum error approximately 2.64e-9. This finite test corroborates only, not proves the full converse.
residual_risks: Finite checks do not prove all parameters; universal proof depends on the mathematical lemmas and hypotheses explicitly reconstructed in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: Cauchy-Crofton normalization, triangle inclusion-exclusion and law of cosines are classical individual tools. Harutyunyan–Ohanyan 2009 and Bäsel 2012 derive chord-length laws mainly for regular polygons, not labeled local-edge hit marginals plus adjacent joint-event inversion for all strictly convex polygons. Gates characterizes triangle/quadrilateral from richer whole chord-length distributions. The complete sparse inverse and global feasibility criterion are a distinct theorem on inspected evidence; residual older side-pair integral geometry priority remains.

Explicit inverse, global feasibility and nondegenerate stability establish substantially more than routine side-length formulas, and the equilateral q-only reduction is a motivated special subclass.
